title: Real Problems, Real Solutions: A Messaging Guide to Move Beyond Racial Scapegoating in the Victorian Election
content:
This message guide has been developed by Common Cause Australia in partnership with the Asylum Seeker Resource Centre and Democracy in Colour, with additional input from GetUp, Victorian Trades Hall Council, and Australian Progress.

This is an interim guide based on early research with persuadable audiences carried out by Common Cause Australia as part of a larger forthcoming project on framing migration in Australia. It is designed for organisations communicating with the public in the run-up to the Victorian Election in November 2026. In addition to our own early research, this interim guide draws on research carried out by GetUp, Victorian Trades Hall Council and ACTU, who kindly shared recent insights.

During elections, debates about migration, multiculturalism, refugees and people seeking asylum can become particularly heightened. Racial scapegoating and divisive rhetoric can become more prominent in public debate.

title: Scenario Planning: Civil Society Responses to Far Right Authoritarianism
content:
This is a scenario planning tool for civil society organisations concerned about whether they have the right strategies in place given the rise of the authoritarian far right and the influence it is already having.

The tool was developed by Jim Coe, UK social movement researcher and consultant. Jim Coe and Natasha Adams have convened gatherings; undertaken research; and produced reports investigating the impact of the far right on civil society organisations, and the range of potential responses.

In their report, Towards Meaningful Action: NGOs’ responses to threats from far-right authoritarianism, Coe and Adams emphasise the need to take substantive steps across a range of areas: Building a collective response; Organisations’ capabilities and preparedness; and Organisational strategy.

The problem we are facing is that a far-right, authoritarian political party is increasingly gaining access to power and could potentially form a future government, but also that the influence of the far-right is already permeating government and other policy, discourse, and spaces for influence. – Towards Meaningful Action, 2026
